9f116d64d4e1: MultiDatePick for Salesforce Developers and Architects
bf096f7f980c: MultiDatePick for developers: where configs live (Custom Metadata), Screen Flow outputs, Apex-defined types for loops, user-mode security and sandbox to production.
766da0fc25b7: Do I need to write Apex to use MultiDatePick?
d5247aa0e78c: No. The components load and save records themselves, and flows that save on their own use the packaged Parse Date Entries from JSON action instead of custom Apex.
3a953879bc45: Yes. Each config is a Custom Metadata record (Config__mdt, plus Config_Extension__mdt for newer settings), so it deploys like any other metadata.
f48e4003256f: Does MultiDatePick add objects for my data?
c6efa87a600c: Only if you want them. It saves to the objects you choose, so your records, automation and reports stay where they are. The package also installs ready-made objects (MDP Schedule, MDP Resource, MDP Event, MDP Sub Block and Office Closure) you can use instead.
0e6510882db6: How does it handle time zones and languages?
e2ed7a571368: Dates and times follow each user's Salesforce time zone and locale, and the interface is translated into nine languages.
99516605de5a: How the calendar fits into your org: where settings live, what a Screen Flow gets back, the Apex types your flows can loop, how security works, and how to move configs between orgs.
f6f4d13d78ee: MultiDatePick is built so admins never need a developer. This page is for the times a developer or architect is involved anyway: reviewing the package, building flows around it, or moving its setup through sandboxes.
3f20aa2beef3: Pick many dates, drag ranges, add recurring patterns. Saves one record per date or per range, or returns the dates to a Screen Flow.
4b2b8075dbb1: Dates plus time slots, shared or per date, with conflict checks. Saves one record per date, per time block, or a parent with sub-blocks.
47ccd414ac8d: Book rooms, equipment, vehicles or people (any object, including User) with capacity, business hours, blocked days and booking rules.
7b0bd53d8e32: A Lightning tab that writes configs, with a live preview and JSON import and export.
762073fde813: <t1>Parse Date Entries from JSON</t1> and <t2>Format MultiDatePick Time Range</t2>, for flows that save the records themselves.
b500b9d56fce: MultiDatePick - Setup, MultiDatePick - User, MultiDatePick - All Access, and MultiDatePick - Guest for public sites.
b3759b238c0f: Every saved setup is a <t1>Custom Metadata</t1> record: <t2>Config__mdt</t2> holds the settings, and <t3>Config_Extension__mdt</t3> holds newer ones as JSON in <t4>Settings__c</t4>. A placement on a page or a flow screen names its config in <t5>Config Name</t5>; any property you also set on the placement overrides the config's text and number values.
9c54e314a07e: <t1>Deployable:</t1> configs are metadata, so they move with change sets, the Salesforce CLI or your CI/CD pipeline like any other metadata.
8c102835aa19: <t1>Portable:</t1> the wizard exports a config as JSON and imports it into another org, mapping any object or field that is missing there.
de32b9347f8f: <t1>Reviewable:</t1> one record per setup, readable in Setup, so a change shows up in a diff.
d6623a60d8ff: The calendar reads and writes your own objects, or the ready-made ones the package installs if you prefer. There is nothing to sync, no external service and no callout: picks become ordinary records on the object you choose, with the fields you map (date, end date, start and end time, status, name, resource). Triggers, flows, validation rules and reports on those objects keep working as usual.
7226be9f6291: Put a component on a flow screen, set Config Name, and read these after the screen:
7f7d77ab6ddc: Each picked date as <t1>YYYY-MM-DD</t1>. Loop it to create one record per date.
db0d9041a059: Picked ranges, each with a start and end date. Always filled.
fd632423abea: Dates & Times component: each date with its start and end time.
a2529a2a3a24: Resource Booking component: how many bookings the save created.
4cfab7be048a: Resource Booking component: dates the save skipped because of a conflict.
447e2652d8f4: Dates & Times with breaks: each day's gaps, for a loop that creates the break records.
fb243a14c325: Pass a record into <t1>Parent Record Id</t1> and the calendar shows that record's existing dates and can save new ones itself. To have the flow save instead, choose <t2>My flow saves them</t2> in the wizard: the calendar then hides its own Save button and only hands the picks to the flow. Resource Booking has no such choice: it always saves its own bookings. With a Relationship Field set, they go to the record in <t3>Parent Record Id</t3>, so bind it: left empty, it shows a setup message and books nothing. With no Relationship Field, it books them linked to no record.

7ec7ebe7a114: The <t1>Screen Flow Guide</t1> walks through the loop step by step, and the <t2>Flow loops post</t2> has three starter flows you can <t3>deploy with VS Code</t3>.
cf825bfdbe35: Every query that returns records, and every save, runs in <t1>user mode</t1>: object permissions, field-level security and sharing apply to the person using the calendar, including guest users on public sites. A few checks run in system mode and return only numbers, never records: capacity and conflict counts that include bookings the user cannot see (so nobody double books a slot they cannot read), the running user's own permission set count, and a row lock before a booking saves.
ae7850cb6e4c: Nothing leaves the org: no callouts, no external servers, no subprocessors.
55dcecd3db5f: Passed the <t1>Salesforce Security Review</t1>. Details on the <t2>Trust & Security</t2> page.
d0553ea1da38: Accessibility: a VPAT 2.5 report against WCAG 2.1 A and AA, on the <t1>Accessibility</t1> page.
